Tony: Hey team — noticed my March net pay is lower than expected after I relocated to the UK. I moved from CA on 2026-02-20. My payslip still shows CA state tax withheld and PTO cashout looks full-month instead of prorated. Can someone confirm what's supposed to happen? Payroll ref 1234-5678.
Ana (People Ops): Sorry you're seeing that, Tony. Can you DM a screenshot of the paystub? Did you complete the international move checklist + tax questionnaire? :thinking_face:
Tony: Sent DM with stub. I completed the relocation checklist on 2026-02-21 and updated my home address and bank on 2026-02-25 in the HR portal. Not sure about the residency end date field.
Raj (Payroll): Thanks — I'm pulling the payrun. System shows 'CA resident' flagged for the 2026-03-01 run because residency end date was blank. That explains the CA withholding. We'll need to reverse the state withholding and process a refund adjustment. Ticketing it now.
Lisa (People Ops): Quick note — for international moves we require the 'residency end date' + the tax questionnaire completed. If that field is empty the payroll system defaults to prior state. If Tony confirms the end date we'll escalate.
Tony: I must've missed that field. My last day in CA was 2026-02-20. I did mark "moved" in the portal but maybe didn't fill the date.
Raj (Payroll): OK. I'll create PAY-2026-432 and set residency end 2026-02-20. Plan: 1) Reverse CA withholding via adjustment in the next payroll (2026-03-15 run), 2) Issue supplemental refund line so you have a clear transaction for mortgage docs, 3) Prepare state correction (W-2C) if needed after month close.
Tony: Will the refund show as a separate transaction or will it adjust the original paycheck? I need a clear statement for mortgage underwriter.
Raj (Payroll): It will be a separate supplemental adjustment line and we'll attach a payroll statement/letter. We'll CC you on the ticket and include amounts and tax codes.
Ana (People Ops): Adding benefits note: international move may trigger benefits enrollment changes. Benefits team will reach out; coverage typically runs through month-end unless you change it.
Tony: And PTO? The cashout was for full-month accrual but I only worked half of the period. Will that be corrected?
Lisa (People Ops): PTO cashout should be prorated by days worked in the pay period. If the full amount hit, payroll will correct the PTO payout line in the adjustment run. If you still have accrual on your balance we'll reconcile.
Raj (Payroll): Confirmed — PTO prorate will be applied on supplemental adjustment. I'll also add a line in the ticket explaining how it will appear on your statement. Ticket: PAY-2026-432 (status: in progress). ETA for adjustments: next payroll cycle 2026-03-15, and we'll follow-up with timeline for W-2/W-2C.
Tony: Thank you. One last Q — will this create double withholding (CA + UK) for Feb/March? How will UK PAYE be applied retroactively?
Raj (Payroll): Possible temporary overlap. We'll set UK payroll start date 2026-02-22 to minimize gap; HMRC reporting may require retroactive submissions, payroll ops will coordinate with our international payroll partner. If double withholding occurs, refund/credit will address it.
payroll-bot: Ticket PAY-2026-432 updated by Raj (Payroll) — status: in progress.
Tony: Appreciate the fast response. Please include a short statement for my mortgage underwriter when you have it.
Raj (Payroll): Will do — we'll attach the statement and CC you when the adjustment posts. :+1:
